What is different about planning an event in Victoria?

Victoria's event market is unusually concentrated. Melbourne holds almost all of the state's working planners, and the regions people actually hold events in, the Yarra Valley and the Mornington Peninsula, sit roughly an hour outside it in opposite directions. That single geography explains most Victorian quotes: the planner is coming from the city, and the suppliers are too.

That concentration is why searches for event planners VIC wide and searches for Melbourne return much the same set of businesses. Party planners Melbourne, wedding planners and event coordinators VIC wide are largely the same people wearing different hats.

The other constant is weather. A Melbourne event in any month needs a plan that works in 18 degrees and rain as well as 34 and sun, and the version that gets used is decided on the morning. Planners here are practised at it, which is why a good Victorian run sheet has a decision point and a deadline written into it rather than a vague hope.

On the ground

What planning in Victoria actually involves

01

Spring racing compresses everything

From late October the carnival takes venues, marquees, staff and hire stock out of circulation across the city. A November event competes with it for the same suppliers, and prices reflect that.

02

Raw venues arrive empty

A warehouse in Collingwood or Cremorne usually comes with four walls and power. Furniture, kitchen, bar, bathrooms, lighting and staff are all separate bookings, which is exactly the situation a planner earns their fee in.

03

An hour out is a different quote

Yarra Valley and Mornington Peninsula events add supplier travel in both directions, and for a Saturday most planners will build in a night of accommodation rather than drive home at 1am.

Timing

When to start planning in Victoria

Melbourne runs to a tighter calendar than most people expect, because the spring carnival and the wine regions compete for the same suppliers on the same weekends.

The wet weather plan is the one to settle early

Book the alternative space at the same time as the main one, not later. A Melbourne venue that says it can move you inside is worth confirming in writing, with a stated capacity and a decision deadline on the day.

Questions

Planning an event in Victoria

How much does an event planner cost in Melbourne?

Airtasker, in a guide updated in February 2025, puts Australian event planning between $1,000 and $20,000 with a national median near $8,000, and notes a common model of 10 to 15 per cent of total event spend. Melbourne sits close to that median for a full plan. The level of service you choose moves the number far more than the suburb does.

Do I need a wet weather plan for a Melbourne event?

Yes, and it needs to be a real one with a decision deadline. Melbourne can move 15 degrees in an afternoon and a southerly change arrives faster than a marquee can be re-rigged. A workable plan names the alternative space, the cut-off time for calling it, and the person who makes that call, which is normally your coordinator rather than you.

Will a Melbourne planner work in the Yarra Valley?

Most will, and many work there monthly. Both the Yarra Valley and the Mornington Peninsula are around an hour from the city, so expect a travel fee and, for a Saturday, accommodation. The more useful question is how many site visits are included, because a venue you cannot drop into on a weeknight changes how the planning runs.

Is there a Victorian planner outside Melbourne?

There are planners in Geelong, Ballarat, Bendigo and the wine regions, but the numbers are small and they book out early for peak weekends. If your date is a Saturday between October and April, start with the local planners and keep a Melbourne option open rather than assuming one will be free.
